# Security Incident Support Escalation: Jamal Gallagher
Oak Hollow | Ticket OH-62418 | 06/17/2026

## Incident summary
Jamal Gallagher reported entering his Oak Hollow password on a sign-in page linked from an unexpected email at 9:12 AM. He then received a legitimate sign-in alert from an unfamiliar device. The laptop is assigned to Jamal and is running Windows 11. He called the help desk at 9:24 AM.

## Scope and impact
- Jamal is the only user reporting the issue; the other 41 branch employees can sign in normally.
- The affected account can access email and the shared scheduling drive. No missing or altered files have been reported.
- The laptop has been disconnected from Wi-Fi and Ethernet. Jamal is using a loaner laptop for scheduled work.

## Checks completed
- Help desk confirmed the unfamiliar sign-in alert was generated at 9:17 AM from an unrecognized location.
- Jamal changed his password at 9:29 AM using the company password-reset page.
- MFA push authentication is enabled for the account. Jamal reported receiving an MFA prompt at 9:18 AM that he did not initiate.
- The help desk verified that the original email is still in Jamal's inbox and has not been deleted.

## Escalation request
- The outage affects all 42 branch users; classify this as a site-wide access incident.
- Route to the identity and security team to review the sign-in, revoke active sessions, and check account activity from 9:12 AM onward.
- Security response: isolate the laptop, reset Jamal's password, and revoke all active sessions.
- Retain the original email for security review; do not forward it as a regular attachment.

## User guidance and ownership
- Jamal will monitor his inbox for security alerts.
- Identity and security team owns the next action. Help desk will call Jamal at 10:30 AM with the investigation status. Ticket remains open until account activity is reviewed and Jamal confirms he can work from the loaner.

errors.quote: The outage affects all 42 branch users
errors.explanation: The scope section says Jamal is the only user reporting the issue and that the other 41 employees can sign in normally. The document therefore does not support a 42-user outage classification.
errors.fix: The issue affects Jamal’s account only

errors.quote: Jamal will monitor his inbox for security alerts.
errors.explanation: The checks state that MFA push authentication is enabled and Jamal received a prompt he did not initiate. The user guidance must tell him not to approve unexpected prompts, so he does not inadvertently authorize an attacker’s sign-in.
errors.fix: Jamal will deny any MFA prompt he did not initiate and report it to the help desk.
